NoteRegexAccessor::search¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note NoteRegexAccessor::search(std::string_view pattern) const

Test Whether A Pattern Occurs Anywhere In A Cell¶

search(pattern) reports, for each cell, whether pattern matches somewhere in the cell — unanchored, the regex analogue of Note::contains. Use it to flag cells that contain a shape (a date, a URL, a code) without caring where in the cell it appears or what surrounds it.

The difference from match is anchoring: search(R"(\d+)") is 1 for "year 2026", match(R"(\d+)") is 0 for it (the whole cell is not digits).

pattern is an ECMAScript regular expression. An invalid pattern throws pluss::Error before any cell is tested.

Return value¶

A Bool Note with the receiver’s shape, one native truth value per cell. Use bools() for a borrowed contiguous host view.

Example 1: Unanchored — Match Anywhere¶

const auto n = pluss::make_note({"2026", "year 2026", "none"});
const auto mask = n.regex().search(R"(\d+)");
std::cout << "[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < mask.bools().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << static_cast<int>(mask.bools()[i]);
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

[1, 1, 0]

Both "2026" and "year 2026" contain a digit run.

See Also¶

  • NoteRegexAccessor::match: the whole-cell, anchored version.

  • Note::contains: a literal (non-regex) “occurs anywhere” test.

  • NoteRegexAccessor::findall: return the matches, not just a yes/no.
